page: Amazon Web Services m6in.24xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 96 vCPUs and 48 physical cores, utilizing the Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz. The system includes 384.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage.

The instance is equipped with a baseline network bandwidth of 150 Gbps. In benchmark testing, the m6in.24xlarge demonstrates strong multi-core CPU performance, as evidenced by its top-25% rankings in stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth is also highly efficient, scoring in the top 25% for both small-block cached and large-block uncached read operations. It also achieves strong results in database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput.

While multi-threaded and memory-intensive tasks perform exceptionally well, single-core performance remains in the average tier across Geekbench and stress-ng tests. Additionally, large-scale LLM text generation represents a notable bottleneck, with the 70B model text generation benchmark falling into the bottom 25%. Given these characteristics, the instance is suited for high-throughput network applications, multi-threaded database operations, web serving, and software compilation, rather than single-threaded tasks or large-scale LLM text generation.
